source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_C::U21: Select the income-tax law and period before applying historical terminology

payload.title: The filing date alone does not identify the governing tax law
payload.core_explanation_md:
The textbook explains the 1961 Act using previous year and assessment year. The Income Tax Department transition FAQ identifies the 2025 Act from1April2026 and the Tax Year terminology for income of2026-27 onwards, while preserving the described earlier-period proceedings. A return filed after commencement can still concern an earlier income period.

Before using an old section number or form, record the income period, governing Act and applicable saving. Residence and source remain separate analytical questions; citizenship, account label and tax residence must not be treated as interchangeable. The textbook legacy rates and section references are research context, not an unqualified current filing guide.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a filing after1April2026 automatically mean every matter uses only the new Act?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The income period and statutory savings matter.

payload.stem_md: A return is filed after the new Act commencement but relates entirely to an earlier income period covered by the saving. What selects the law?

payload.stem_md: A tax memo infers residence only from citizenship. What is the missing step?

options.text_md: Apply the statutory residence/source rules to the actual person and period
options.explanation_md: Citizenship and tax residence are not identical tests.

options.text_md: Assume every foreign receipt is exempt for every category
Treat account balance as the residence definition
options.explanation_md: Wealth does not alone establish residence.
